steps.title: Rows and columns
steps.content: A matrix is a rectangular arrangement of values. An r×c matrix has r rows and c columns. In a 2D array, an element is accessed with a row index and a column index.
steps.example: A 2×3 matrix has 2 rows and 3 columns, for 6 values total.

steps.title: Count matrix elements
steps.prompt: How many elements are in a 3×4 matrix?

steps.title: Transpose a matrix
steps.content: The transpose swaps rows and columns. An element at row i, column j moves to row j, column i. A matrix with r rows and c columns becomes c×r.

steps.title: Check multiplication dimensions
steps.prompt: A 2×3 matrix is multiplied by a 3×4 matrix. What is the result's dimension?
steps.explanation: The inner dimensions (3 and 3) match; the result uses the outer dimensions 2×4.

steps.title: Use nested loops carefully
steps.content: Matrix traversal usually uses an outer loop for rows and an inner loop for columns. Matrix addition requires equal dimensions; matrix multiplication requires the first matrix's columns to equal the second matrix's rows.
steps.tip: Write the matrix dimensions beside the problem before coding.

questions.prompt: How many elements are in a 4×5 matrix?
What are the dimensions of the transpose of a 2×5 matrix?
questions.explanation: Transpose swaps rows and columns, giving 5×2.

questions.prompt: Can a 2×3 matrix be added to a 3×2 matrix?
options: Only if all values are zero
questions.explanation: Matrix addition requires the same number of rows and columns.

questions.prompt: What is the result dimension of (3×2) × (2×5)?
questions.explanation: The inner dimensions match (2), and the result has the outer dimensions 3×5.

questions.prompt: Which index pair identifies a value in a 2D array?
questions.explanation: A 2D array element is addressed by both its row and column indices.
